steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Procurement is the process of sourcing and purchasing materials: choosing reliable suppliers who offer the right quality, price, and delivery times. | Key Fact: Buffer stock is the minimum level of stock a business holds to prevent running out if demand unexpectedly increases or supply is delayed - a safety net. | Key Fact: Just-in-time (JIT) stock control means ordering stock to arrive only when needed: eliminates storage costs but requires reliable suppliers and accurate demand forecasting. | Key Fact: The bar gate stock control chart shows: maximum stock level, buffer stock level, re-order level (when to order), and lead time (time between ordering and delivery).

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the difference between buffer stock and just-in-time stock management. | Describe the key features of a bar gate stock control chart and explain why it is useful. | Evaluate whether a restaurant should use JIT stock control.
